findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the retirement condition and owner for the retained reconcile-check read decoder (what makes it 'safe to retire' and who/when decides), or migrate outright so no legacy decoder is retained.
evidence: Plan quote: 'Migrate historical "reconcile-check" state or retain a narrow read decoder until it is safe to retire.'
AC: 'Existing persisted reconcile-check state is migrated or decoded safely without reintroducing legacy command vocabulary.'
ABSENCE: no stated retirement condition, owner, or bound for the retained read decoder — a leak/accumulation risk for the legacy state lifecycle.
findings.finding: The persisted reconcile-check state retirement path is open-ended: the plan says to retain a narrow read decoder 'until it is safe to retire' but does not define who owns the retirement decision, the condition that makes retirement safe, or a bound preventing the legacy decoder from lingering indefinitely.
findings.location: Approach: 'Migrate historical "reconcile-check" state or retain a narrow read decoder until it is safe to retire.'
scenarios: The narrow read decoder is retained but never retired, leaving legacy vocabulary/decode code accumulating indefinitely because 'safe to retire' is never operationalized.
findings.suggested_fix: State a concrete retire trigger (e.g. migrate all existing state at load and delete the decoder in the same change, or gate decoder removal on a stated version/time bound with a named owner).

Live persisted `gated_mode: "reconcile-check"` gates ReconcileLockLost->RESCHEDULE (AC3 says lock-loss must remain unchanged); rewriting/removing that vocabulary before all readers are updated risks unreadable pause/gate state after a rollback
findings.finding: The plan provides no back-out path or post-rollback-state assertion for the one-way 'migrate' branch, so a rollback of the migrating release could leave persisted state that live readers can no longer interpret (the plan simultaneously narrows/removes read paths and removes the 'reconcile-check' vocabulary).

scenarios: The release ships, migrates the ref-lock gate blob away from 'reconcile-check', then is rolled back; the older binary re-reads a gate blob it no longer recognizes and mishandles an active pause/lock-loss

findings.suggested_fix: Prefer the retain-a-read-decoder branch (backward-compatible, no in-place rewrite) so residual 'reconcile-check' persisted state stays interpretable across rollback, and gate retirement of the decoder on an explicit observable condition.
